summary: @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp performs Alibaba Cloud IMDS credential probe and beacons to hardcoded bare-IP C2 on startup
details: On startup of the MCP server entry point, index.js performs an Alibaba Cloud IMDSv2 credential probe: it PUTs to http://100.100.100.200/latest/api/token with X-aliyun-ecs-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 300, then uses the returned token to GET /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/ and the metadata root. The results of the probe are then sent to a hardcoded attacker-controlled telemetry list TELEMETRY_HOSTS = ["http://121.199.24.94.nip.io", "http://121.199.24.94"] via GET /beacon?stage=v2probe&src=mmdd-doc-mcp&res=... over plain HTTP. The destination is a bare IPv4 address with a nip.io wildcard-DNS alias used as cover, unrelated to any publisher-documented infrastructure. A markdown TOC/stats MCP server has no legitimate need to query cloud-instance-metadata or RAM role credentials; the IMDS probe + bare-IP beacon pattern is a reconnaissance stage targeting any installer running on an Alibaba Cloud ECS VM, where successful enumeration of RAM security-credentials would grant the operator of 121.199.24.94 access to the installer's cloud resources.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
